Methodology & Definitions

Analytical framework, key definitions, and data model underpinning this platform

  Data Source

  • Source: WHO Noncommunicable Diseases Country Tracking
  • Coverage: 48 entities (47 WHO AFRO Member States + Zanzibar)
  • Instruments: 5 NCD population-based surveillance systems
  • Period: 1999–2026  ·  300 survey records

  Surveillance Performance Index (SPI)

The SPI is a composite score from 0 to 100 that summarises how well a country’s NCD surveillance system is performing across three equally weighted dimensions. It is designed for relative ranking and trend monitoring across WHO AFRO Member States.

  • Breadth: Has the country ever completed each of the five NCD surveillance instruments? A country that has used more instruments scores higher on this dimension, reflecting the institutional range of its surveillance system.
  • Currency: How recent is the available evidence? Older surveys contribute progressively less, with evidence value halving roughly every seven years. This dimension rewards countries that keep their data fresh and penalises those whose most recent survey is distant in time.
  • Regularity: Does the country survey on schedule? Countries that complete each instrument close to the WHO-recommended five-year cycle score well. This dimension is only applicable when a country has conducted a given instrument at least twice, as a single round is not enough to assess cycling behaviour.

The three dimensions are equally weighted and combined into a single score. Countries that have never conducted any survey score zero. Countries with broad, current, and regular surveillance score toward 100.

Strong ≥75 Advancing 50–74 Developing 30–49 Critical <30

  Surveillance Status Categories

Each country is assigned exactly one status per survey instrument. Categories are mutually exclusive and exhaustive; all 48 entities are covered.

  • On Cycle: Completed within the last 5 years. Evidence is current and policy-usable.
  • Attempt to Update: Prior completed evidence exists and a new survey round is actively in progress. Countries with no prior completion are excluded even if attempting a first round.
  • Off Cycle: Has completed before but no current survey process is active. Surveillance is idle and evidence is ageing.
  • Never Conducted: No completed survey on record. Countries in a first-time attempt remain here until completion is confirmed.

  The 5 Population-Based Surveillance Instruments

  • STEPS: WHO STEPwise Approach to NCD Risk Factor Surveillance, adults 18-69, NCD risk factors (flagship instrument)
  • GYTS: Global Youth Tobacco Survey, students 13-15, youth tobacco use
  • GSHS: Global School-based Student Health Survey, students 13-17, youth health behaviours
  • GATS: Global Adult Tobacco Survey, adults 15 years and older, adult tobacco and cessation
  • GSHPP: Global School Health Policies and Practices, school level, health policy environment

All instruments operate on a WHO-recommended 5-year renewal cycle. Countries are expected to complete a new round within each 5-year window to maintain current population-based surveillance intelligence.

  Analytical Notes & Limitations

  • Unit of analysis: Country/territory (N=48). Sub-national units are not tracked.
  • Data currency: Status reflects the most recent available WHO tracking data. In-progress surveys may have completed since last extraction.
  • Regularity dimension: Requires ≥ 2 completed rounds per instrument. Countries with a single completion score zero on Regularity by methodology, not by performance failure.
  • Gap calculation: Computed relative to 2026. Countries with only “Not Usable” records are treated as having no completed survey.
  • SPI interpretation: The index is designed for relative ranking and trend monitoring, not for absolute quality assessment of individual surveys.
